newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Expelled Afghan leader leaves Pakistani city.
newsitem.headline: Expelled Afghan leader leaves Pakistani city.

text.p: A former Afghan provincial governor left for Germany on Monday, obeying a Pakistani expulsion order as Afghanistan's Taleban militia reported the death of his son in battle.
Haji Abdul Qadeer, a former governor of Afghanistan's eastern province of Nangarhar, left Peshawar for Karachi and was due to fly to Germany via Dubai, family sources said.

Qadeer told reporters on Sunday that Pakistan had asked him and a colleague to leave the country because of their activities against the Taleban, which controls two-thirds of war-shattered Afghanistan. Kabul radio said on Monday that Qadeer's son Zahir was in a group killed fighting against the Taleban and that their bodies were paraded on vehicles in the Nangarhar province capital of Jalalabad. The Taleban-controlled radio did not say when the battle took place.
